summary: Original catalogue-wide screen retained and independently spot-checked across all ten SchurWeyl stages; the five subsequently added roadmaps were screened, giving 217 other roadmaps in the current 218-roadmap catalogue. All ten narrowly scoped links and seven ownership/interface overlaps are retained after full endpoint reading and literal-quote verification; overlap 5 now reuses the pinned semisimple image-bicommutant theorem rather than requesting its reconstruction. No additional exact supplier/consumer match was established. The recorded coefficient, image-algebra, convention and missing-target obligations remain open roadmap work, not certified theorems.

overlaps.detail: Both SchurWeyl Layer 8 and ClassicalGroups Layers 2/4 construct Young-image Schur modules and identify their characters, while ClassicalGroups explicitly assigns the GL_n image to itself. Whole-stage imports in both directions would make the shared construction circular.
overlaps.proposal: Keep SchurWeyl Layer 2 as the unique symmetrizer supplier and Layer 7 as the finite-polynomial supplier. Share one early equivariant Young-image constructor (maintain the ClassicalGroups Layer 2 ownership clause), prove the SchurWeyl multiplicity-space/image comparison separately, and keep highest-weight/rational-character identification in ClassicalGroups. Until declaration-sized subtargets exist, use only the recorded SchurWeyl-to-ClassicalGroups edges; do not add the reverse whole-stage edge.

overlaps.detail: ClassicalGroups Layer 4 lists bialternant, Pieri and Littlewood-Richardson identities as SchurWeyl exports, and LieHighestWeight Layer 6 assigns general Littlewood-Richardson coefficients there. The actual SchurWeyl Layer 7 targets specify finite Schur polynomials/Jacobi-Trudi/RSK and mention Pieri as a route, but do not pin the full advertised contracts.
overlaps.proposal: Request explicit finite-variable bialternant with divisibility, Pieri and Littlewood-Richardson statements and their coefficient/index conventions from SchurWeyl before adding edges for them. Keep the minuscule Lie-theoretic Pieri theorem in LieHighestWeight; it is not a proof of the general combinatorial rule. Remove ClassicalGroups Ordering's competing claim to rebuild the Schur-function foundation.

overlaps.detail: ClassicalGroups Layer 6 attributes the bounded-tableau/Gelfand-Tsetlin-pattern dictionary to SchurWeyl, but no such dictionary is a SchurWeyl stage target. RSK and the standard-tableau pair correspondence are different results.
overlaps.proposal: Keep finite-alphabet semistandard tableau and Schur-polynomial objects in SchurWeyl. Assign the interlacing-pattern/bounded-tableau equivalence to ClassicalGroups Layer 6, with bounds imposed only on diagram cells, and add the rational determinant-shift extension there. Do not create a purported RSK-to-GT theorem dependency.

overlaps.detail: Both roadmaps need the complex orthogonal/symplectic standard action. ClassicalGroups names Matrix.orthogonalGroup, whereas SchurWeyl explicitly demands the complex symmetric-bilinear group and warns against the Hermitian/unitary interpretation. This is a source-level convention conflict, not a verified claim about the pinned library declaration.
overlaps.proposal: Choose one group of automorphisms preserving the specified nondegenerate complex bilinear form, its GL inclusion and invariant pairing. Prove any matrix-group comparison before reuse. Keep Brauer diagram actions and image-centralizer theorems in SchurWeyl, and classical highest-weight/branching consumers in ClassicalGroups. Repair the symplectic generator sign convention before asserting a Brauer-action interface.

overlaps.detail: The source descriptions overlap at density and tensor commutants, but SA3 states a simple-module result whereas SW8 needs a semisimple image theorem. This is a documentary mismatch, not an unbuilt intermediate theorem: the pinned TauCeti already supplies centralizer_centralizer_range for the image of a semisimple algebra on a finite base module, without faithful action.
overlaps.proposal: Reuse TauCeti.centralizer_centralizer_range in TauCeti/RingTheory/Semisimple/DoubleCentralizer.lean at f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369. Its parameters are a commutative base ring K, a K-module N with Module.Finite K N, a semisimple K-algebra S and an algebra map S -> End_K(N); it returns the double centralizer of the image as that image. Align SA3 with this existing output instead of requesting a new block/multiplicity proof. SW8 still must identify the GL image/span with the full S_n commutant before applying the theorem. No unconditional SA3-to-SW8 edge is submitted.

overlaps.detail: Both stages maintain cycle-type data for finite permutations including fixed points: SchurWeyl uses partitions to index conjugacy classes, while PolynomialGaloisGroups exports fullCycleType as a multiset. This is a common finite-permutation adapter, not a dependency on arithmetic factorization or Specht representation theory.
overlaps.proposal: Keep the fullCycleType multiset API with PolynomialGaloisGroups and the partition/conjugacy-class equivalence with SchurWeyl. Request one natural comparison between the underlying partition multiset and fullCycleType, checked on the empty set, identity and a transposition. Neither whole stage should be required as a prerequisite of the other merely to define this adapter.

overlaps.detail: The generic Dixon-Schneider solver and the Murnaghan-Nakayama recursion independently compute symmetric-group character tables; S_3 and S_4 are shared acceptance examples. Neither algorithm requires the other as a theorem input.
overlaps.proposal: Reuse CharacterTheory Layer 5's specification and explicit row/column transports to compare their outputs on shared examples. Keep the generic cyclotomic solver separate from SchurWeyl's integral partition recursion; add test-fixture comparisons only after both are constructed, not a reverse algorithm dependency.
